alt: A side view of a tropical cyclone over warm sea with a calm eye. Warm moist air from sea that is at least 27 degrees Celsius and at least 60 metres deep rises, cools and condenses, releasing heat that drives the storm. A spiral from above shows the spin that needs distance from the equator. Over land the storm loses its energy supply and weakens.
caption: A cyclone feeds on warm sea water and weakens over land or colder water.
